passages.text: Now the LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, “This month is the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of your year.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
They were in the land of Egypt.
The LORD said, “This month will be your beginning of months.
This month will be the first month of your year.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֔ן בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לֵאמֹֽר׃ הַחֹ֧דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם רֹ֣אשׁ חֳדָשִׁ֑ים רִאשׁ֥וֹן הוּא֙ לָכֶ֔ם לְחָדְשֵׁ֖י הַשָּׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: Tell the whole congregation of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each man must select a lamb for his family, one per household.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses and Aaron in Egypt.
God gave them instructions for the Israelites.
God said, “Speak to the whole congregation of Israel.”
God said, “On the tenth day of this month, each man must choose a lamb.”
Each man must choose a lamb for his family.
Each household must have one lamb.
passages.original: דַּבְּר֗וּ אֶֽל־ כָּל־ עֲדַ֤ת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בֶּעָשֹׂ֖ר לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וְיִקְח֣וּ לָהֶ֗ם אִ֛ישׁ שֶׂ֥ה לְבֵית־ אָבֹ֖ת שֶׂ֥ה לַבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: If the household is too small for a whole lamb, they are to share with the nearest neighbor based on the number of people, and apportion the lamb accordingly.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses and Aaron in Egypt.
God gave instructions for the people of Israel.
If a family is too small to eat a whole lamb,
the family must join with their nearest neighbor.
They must count the number of people in both households.
They must divide the lamb according to how much each person will eat.
Each person should receive a fair share of the lamb.
passages.original: וְאִם־ יִמְעַ֣ט הַבַּיִת֮ מִהְיֹ֣ת מִשֶּׂה֒ וְלָקַ֣ח ה֗וּא וּשְׁכֵנ֛וֹ הַקָּרֹ֥ב אֶל־ בֵּית֖וֹ בְּמִכְסַ֣ת נְפָשֹׁ֑ת אִ֚ישׁ לְפִ֣י אָכְל֔וֹ תָּכֹ֖סּוּ עַל־ הַשֶּֽׂה׃

passages.text: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male, and you may take it from the sheep or the goats.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
He gave them instructions for the Passover sacrifice.
Each family must choose a lamb.
The lamb must be a male.
The lamb must be one year old.
The lamb must have no blemish.
The lamb can be from the sheep.
The lamb can also be from the goats.
passages.original: שֶׂ֥ה תָמִ֛ים זָכָ֥ר בֶּן־ שָׁנָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם מִן־ הַכְּבָשִׂ֥ים וּמִן־ הָעִזִּ֖ים תִּקָּֽחוּ׃

passages.text: You must keep it until the fourteenth day of the month, when the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel will slaughter the animals at twilight.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions to the Israelites.
God told them to take a lamb or a goat.
The animal must be a year-old male without blemish.
They must keep the animal until the fourteenth day of the month.
On the fourteenth day, the Israelites must gather together.
The whole assembly of Israel must slaughter the animal.
They must do this at twilight.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה לָכֶם֙ לְמִשְׁמֶ֔רֶת עַ֣ד אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וְשָׁחֲט֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ כֹּ֛ל קְהַ֥ל עֲדַֽת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: They are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites must take some of the lamb’s blood.
They must put the blood on the sides of the doorframes.
They must also put the blood on the tops of the doorframes.
They must do this on the houses where they eat the lambs.
passages.original: וְלָֽקְחוּ֙ מִן־ הַדָּ֔ם וְנָֽתְנ֛וּ עַל־ שְׁתֵּ֥י הַמְּזוּזֹ֖ת וְעַל־ הַמַּשְׁק֑וֹף עַ֚ל הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ יֹאכְל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: They are to eat the meat that night, roasted over the fire, along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites must eat the meat that night.
They must roast the meat over the fire.
They must eat the meat with unleavened bread.
They must eat the meat with bitter herbs.
passages.original: וְאָכְל֥וּ אֶת־ הַבָּשָׂ֖ר בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַזֶּ֑ה צְלִי־ אֵ֣שׁ וּמַצּ֔וֹת עַל־ מְרֹרִ֖ים יֹאכְלֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Do not eat any of the meat raw or cooked in boiling water, but only roasted over the fire—its head and legs and inner parts.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions for eating the Passover lamb.
Do not eat any of the meat raw.
Do not eat any of the meat cooked in boiling water.
Roast the meat over the fire.
Roast the head, the legs, and the inner parts together.
passages.original: אַל־ תֹּאכְל֤וּ מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ נָ֔א וּבָשֵׁ֥ל מְבֻשָּׁ֖ל בַּמָּ֑יִם כִּ֣י אִם־ צְלִי־ אֵ֔שׁ רֹאשׁ֥וֹ עַל־ כְּרָעָ֖יו וְעַל־ קִרְבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do not leave any of it until morning; before the morning you must burn up any part that is left over.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions for the Passover meal.
He commanded the Israelites.
Do not leave any of the meat until morning.
If any meat is left over before morning, burn it in the fire.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ תוֹתִ֥ירוּ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד־ בֹּ֑קֶר וְהַנֹּתָ֥ר מִמֶּ֛נּוּ עַד־ בֹּ֖קֶר בָּאֵ֥שׁ תִּשְׂרֹֽפוּ׃

passages.text: This is how you are to eat it: You must be fully dressed for travel, with your sandals on your feet and your staff in your hand. You are to eat in haste; it is the LORD’s Passover.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to eat the Passover meal in a special way.
You must wear your belt around your waist.
You must put your sandals on your feet.
You must hold your staff in your hand.
You must eat the meal quickly.
This meal is the LORD’s Passover.
passages.original: וְכָכָה֮ תֹּאכְל֣וּ אֹתוֹ֒ מָתְנֵיכֶ֣ם חֲגֻרִ֔ים נַֽעֲלֵיכֶם֙ בְּרַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וּמַקֶּלְכֶ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ בְּחִפָּז֔וֹן פֶּ֥סַח ה֖וּא לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: On that night I will pass through the land of Egypt and strike down every firstborn male, both man and beast, and I will execute judgment against all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke these words.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said, "On this night I will pass through the land of Egypt."
I will strike down every firstborn in Egypt.
I will strike both people and animals.
I will punish all the gods of Egypt.
I am the LORD.
passages.original: וְעָבַרְתִּ֣י בְאֶֽרֶץ־ מִצְרַיִם֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַזֶּה֒ וְהִכֵּיתִ֤י כָל־ בְּכוֹר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־ בְּהֵמָ֑ה וּבְכָל־ אֱלֹהֵ֥י מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה שְׁפָטִ֖ים אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The blood on the houses where you are staying will distinguish them; when I see the blood, I will pass over you. No plague will fall on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites in Egypt.
God told them to put blood on their houses.
The blood would be a sign on the houses where they stayed.
God said, "When I see the blood, I will pass over you."
No plague will strike you to destroy you.
I will strike the land of Egypt, but you will be safe.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֩ הַדָּ֨ם לָכֶ֜ם לְאֹ֗ת עַ֤ל הַבָּתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם שָׁ֔ם וְרָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ הַדָּ֔ם וּפָסַחְתִּ֖י עֲלֵכֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה בָכֶ֥ם נֶ֙גֶף֙ לְמַשְׁחִ֔ית בְּהַכֹּתִ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: And this day will be a memorial for you, and you are to celebrate it as a feast to the LORD, as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
passages.sermon:
God rescued the Israelites from Egypt on this day.
This day will be a memorial for you.
You must celebrate this day as a feast to the LORD.
You must keep this feast for all your generations.
You must observe it as a permanent statute.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֩ הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֤ה לָכֶם֙ לְזִכָּר֔וֹן וְחַגֹּתֶ֥ם אֹת֖וֹ חַ֣ג לַֽיהוָ֑ה לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם תְּחָגֻּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: For seven days you must eat unleavened bread. On the first day you are to remove the leaven from your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened from the first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to observe a special time.
For seven days, you must eat unleavened bread.
On the first day, you must remove all leaven from your houses.
If anyone eats anything leavened during these seven days, that person must be cut off from Israel.
This rule applies from the first day until the seventh day.
passages.original: שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ מַצּ֣וֹת תֹּאכֵ֔לוּ אַ֚ךְ בַּיּ֣וֹם הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן תַּשְׁבִּ֥יתוּ שְּׂאֹ֖ר מִבָּתֵּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י׀ כָּל־ אֹכֵ֣ל חָמֵ֗ץ וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַהִוא֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִיּ֥וֹם הָרִאשֹׁ֖ן עַד־ י֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִעִֽי׃

passages.text: On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly, and another on the seventh day. You must not do any work on those days, except to prepare the meals—that is all you may do.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
On the first day, you must gather for a sacred assembly.
On the seventh day, you must also gather for a sacred assembly.
You must not do any work on these two days.
You may only prepare food for everyone to eat on these days.
No other work is allowed.
passages.original: וּבַיּ֤וֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ מִקְרָא־ קֹ֔דֶשׁ וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִקְרָא־ קֹ֖דֶשׁ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם כָּל־ מְלָאכָה֙ לֹא־ יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה בָהֶ֔ם אַ֚ךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵאָכֵ֣ל לְכָל־ נֶ֔פֶשׁ ה֥וּא לְבַדּ֖וֹ יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: So you are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt. You must keep this day as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
God brought the Israelites out of Egypt on this day.
God delivered all the people of Israel from slavery in Egypt.
God told the Israelites to remember this day for all generations.
God made this day a permanent law for the people of Israel.
passages.original: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֮ אֶת־ הַמַּצּוֹת֒ כִּ֗י בְּעֶ֙צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶת־ צִבְאוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶ֖ם חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: In the first month you are to eat unleavened bread, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel a command.
God told them about the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
This feast happens in the first month.
Begin eating unleavened bread on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening.
Continue eating unleavened bread until the evening of the twenty-first day of the month.
Eat only unleavened bread during this time.
passages.original: בָּרִאשֹׁ֡ן בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֤וֹם לַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב תֹּאכְל֖וּ מַצֹּ֑ת עַ֠ד י֣וֹם הָאֶחָ֧ד וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ בָּעָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: For seven days there must be no leaven found in your houses. If anyone eats something leavened, that person, whether a foreigner or native of the land, must be cut off from the congregation of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God gave a command to the people of Israel.
He told them about the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
For seven days, they must not have any leaven in their houses.
No one should eat anything leavened during these days.
If anyone eats something leavened, that person will be separated from the congregation of Israel.
This rule applies to everyone.
It applies to both foreigners and natives of the land.
passages.original: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים שְׂאֹ֕ר לֹ֥א יִמָּצֵ֖א בְּבָתֵּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י׀ כָּל־ אֹכֵ֣ל מַחְמֶ֗צֶת וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַהִוא֙ מֵעֲדַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּגֵּ֖ר וּבְאֶזְרַ֥ח הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: You are not to eat anything leavened; eat unleavened bread in all your homes.”
passages.sermon:
God gave a command to the people of Israel.
Do not eat anything leavened.
Eat only unleavened bread.
Do this in every place where you live.
passages.original: כָּל־ מַחְמֶ֖צֶת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ בְּכֹל֙ מוֹשְׁבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם תֹּאכְל֖וּ מַצּֽוֹת׃פ

passages.text: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and told them, “Go at once and select for yourselves a lamb for each family, and slaughter the Passover lamb.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
He called all the elders of Israel.
He spoke to them.
He said, "Go at once."
He told them to select a lamb for each family.
He told them to slaughter the Passover lamb.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה לְכָל־ זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֑ם מִֽשְׁכ֗וּ וּקְח֨וּ לָכֶ֥ם צֹ֛אן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתֵיכֶ֖ם וְשַׁחֲט֥וּ הַפָּֽסַח׃

passages.text: Take a cluster of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin, and brush the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe. None of you shall go out the door of his house until morning.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the elders of Israel.
He gave them instructions for the Passover night.
Take a bunch of hyssop.
Dip the hyssop into the blood in the basin.
Put some of the blood on the top of the doorframe.
Put some of the blood on both sides of the doorframe.
Use the blood from the basin.
Do not go out of your house.
No one should leave through the door until morning.
passages.original: וּלְקַחְתֶּ֞ם אֲגֻדַּ֣ת אֵז֗וֹב וּטְבַלְתֶּם֮ בַּדָּ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ בַּסַּף֒ וְהִגַּעְתֶּ֤ם אֶל־ הַמַּשְׁקוֹף֙ וְאֶל־ שְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּזֹ֔ת מִן־ הַדָּ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּסָּ֑ף וְאַתֶּ֗ם לֹ֥א תֵצְא֛וּ אִ֥ישׁ מִפֶּֽתַח־ בֵּית֖וֹ עַד־ בֹּֽקֶר׃

passages.text: When the LORD passes through to strike down the Egyptians, He will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway; so He will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
\r\nThe LORD will pass through Egypt.
\r\nThe LORD will strike down the Egyptians.
\r\nThe LORD will see the blood on the top of your doorframe.
\r\nThe LORD will see the blood on the sides of your doorframe.
\r\nThe LORD will pass over that doorway.
\r\nThe LORD will not let the destroyer enter your houses.
\r\nThe destroyer will not strike you down.
passages.original: וְעָבַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לִנְגֹּ֣ף אֶת־ מִצְרַיִם֒ וְרָאָ֤ה אֶת־ הַדָּם֙ עַל־ הַמַּשְׁק֔וֹף וְעַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּזֹ֑ת וּפָסַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ עַל־ הַפֶּ֔תַח וְלֹ֤א יִתֵּן֙ הַמַּשְׁחִ֔ית לָבֹ֥א אֶל־ בָּתֵּיכֶ֖ם לִנְגֹּֽף׃

passages.text: And you are to keep this command as a permanent statute for you and your descendants.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to the Israelites.
This command is for you.
This command is for your children.
You must keep this command.
You must keep it always.
This command is a lasting law.
passages.original: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה לְחָק־ לְךָ֥ וּלְבָנֶ֖יךָ עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: When you enter the land that the LORD will give you as He promised, you are to keep this service.
passages.sermon:
The LORD made a promise to you.
He will give you a land.
You will enter that land.
When you enter the land, remember this command.
You must keep this service.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־ תָבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־ הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־ הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: When your children ask you, ‘What does this service mean to you?’
passages.sermon:
Your children may ask you a question.
They may say, “What does this service mean to you?”
They want to know the meaning of this command.
They want to understand why you do this service.
They are asking about the purpose of this practice.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֕ה כִּֽי־ יֹאמְר֥וּ אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בְּנֵיכֶ֑ם מָ֛ה הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: you are to reply, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt when He struck down the Egyptians and spared our homes.’ ” Then the people bowed down and worshiped.
passages.sermon:
This is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD.
The LORD passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt.
The LORD struck down the Egyptians.
The LORD spared our homes.
The people bowed down.
The people worshiped.
passages.original: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֡ם זֶֽבַח־ פֶּ֨סַח ה֜וּא לַֽיהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּ֠סַח עַל־ בָּתֵּ֤י בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם בְּנָגְפּ֥וֹ אֶת־ מִצְרַ֖יִם וְאֶת־ בָּתֵּ֣ינוּ הִצִּ֑יל וַיִּקֹּ֥ד הָעָ֖ם וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ׃

passages.text: And the Israelites went and did just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were God's chosen people.
God gave commands to Moses and Aaron.
Moses and Aaron led the Israelites.
The Israelites listened to Moses and Aaron.
The Israelites went and obeyed.
They did exactly what God commanded through Moses and Aaron.
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃ס

passages.text: Now at midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn male in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on his throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner in the dungeon, as well as all the firstborn among the livestock.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted at midnight.
The LORD struck down every firstborn male in Egypt.
He struck the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on his throne.
He struck the firstborn of the prisoner in the dungeon.
He struck all the firstborn among the livestock.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֗יְלָה וַֽיהוָה֮ הִכָּ֣ה כָל־ בְּכוֹר֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ מִבְּכֹ֤ר פַּרְעֹה֙ הַיֹּשֵׁ֣ב עַל־ כִּסְא֔וֹ עַ֚ד בְּכ֣וֹר הַשְּׁבִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית הַבּ֑וֹר וְכֹ֖ל בְּכ֥וֹר בְּהֵמָֽה׃

passages.text: During the night Pharaoh got up—he and all his officials and all the Egyptians—and there was loud wailing in Egypt; for there was no house without someone dead.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
During the night, Pharaoh got up.
All his officials got up.
All the Egyptians got up.
There was loud wailing in Egypt.
Every house in Egypt had someone dead.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨קָם פַּרְעֹ֜ה לַ֗יְלָה ה֤וּא וְכָל־ עֲבָדָיו֙ וְכָל־ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַתְּהִ֛י צְעָקָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי־ אֵ֣ין בַּ֔יִת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵֽין־ שָׁ֖ם מֵֽת׃

passages.text: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron by night and said, “Get up, leave my people, both you and the Israelites! Go, worship the LORD as you have requested.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
He called for Moses and Aaron during the night.
He spoke to them.
He said, "Get up."
He said, "Leave my people."
He said, "You must go."
He said, "Take the Israelites with you."
He said, "Go and worship the LORD."
He said, "Do as you have asked."
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָא֩ לְמֹשֶׁ֨ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֜ן לַ֗יְלָה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ ק֤וּמוּ צְּאוּ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ עַמִּ֔י גַּם־ אַתֶּ֖ם גַּם־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּלְכ֛וּ עִבְד֥וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה כְּדַבֶּרְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Take your flocks and herds as well, just as you have said, and depart! And bless me also.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to Moses and Aaron at night.
Pharaoh told them to take their flocks.
Pharaoh told them to take their herds.
Pharaoh said they should take everything as they had said.
Pharaoh told them to leave Egypt.
Pharaoh asked them to bless him also.
passages.original: גַּם־ צֹאנְכֶ֨ם גַּם־ בְּקַרְכֶ֥ם קְח֛וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּרְתֶּ֖ם וָלֵ֑כוּ וּבֵֽרַכְתֶּ֖ם גַּם־ אֹתִֽי׃

passages.text: And in order to send them out of the land quickly, the Egyptians urged the people on. “For otherwise,” they said, “we are all going to die!”
passages.sermon:
The Egyptians lived in Egypt.
The Egyptians wanted the Israelites to leave Egypt quickly.
The Egyptians pressed the Israelites to go.
The Egyptians said, “We are all going to die if they stay.”
passages.original: וַתֶּחֱזַ֤ק מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ עַל־ הָעָ֔ם לְמַהֵ֖ר לְשַׁלְּחָ֣ם מִן־ הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֥י אָמְר֖וּ כֻּלָּ֥נוּ מֵתִֽים׃

passages.text: So the people took their dough before it was leavened, carrying it on their shoulders in kneading bowls wrapped in clothing.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were leaving Egypt.
They took their dough with them.
The dough had not risen yet.
They put their kneading bowls in their clothing.
They carried the bowls on their shoulders.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א הָעָ֛ם אֶת־ בְּצֵק֖וֹ טֶ֣רֶם יֶחְמָ֑ץ מִשְׁאֲרֹתָ֛ם צְרֻרֹ֥ת בְּשִׂמְלֹתָ֖ם עַל־ שִׁכְמָֽם׃

passages.text: Furthermore, the Israelites acted on Moses’ word and asked the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold, and for clothing.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were slaves in Egypt.
Moses was their leader.
Moses told the Israelites what to do.
The Israelites obeyed Moses.
They went to the Egyptians.
They asked the Egyptians for silver objects.
They asked the Egyptians for gold objects.
They asked the Egyptians for clothing.
passages.original: וּבְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עָשׂ֖וּ כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַֽיִּשְׁאֲלוּ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם כְּלֵי־ כֶ֛סֶף וּכְלֵ֥י זָהָ֖ב וּשְׂמָלֹֽת׃

passages.text: And the LORD gave the people such favor in the sight of the Egyptians that they granted their request. In this way they plundered the Egyptians.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted for the Israelites.
The LORD made the Egyptians look kindly on the Israelites.
The Egyptians saw the Israelites with favor.
The Israelites asked the Egyptians for items.
The Egyptians gave the Israelites what they asked for.
The Israelites took valuable things from the Egyptians.
The Israelites plundered the Egyptians.
passages.original: וַֽיהוָ֞ה נָתַ֨ן אֶת־ חֵ֥ן הָעָ֛ם בְּעֵינֵ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם וַיַּשְׁאִל֑וּם וַֽיְנַצְּל֖וּ אֶת־ מִצְרָֽיִם׃פ

passages.text: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites left Rameses.
They traveled to Succoth.
About 600,000 men walked with them.
This number does not include women.
This number does not include children.
passages.original: וַיִּסְע֧וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵרַעְמְסֵ֖ס סֻכֹּ֑תָה כְּשֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֨וֹת אֶ֧לֶף רַגְלִ֛י הַגְּבָרִ֖ים לְבַ֥ד מִטָּֽף׃

passages.text: And a mixed multitude also went up with them, along with great droves of livestock, both flocks and herds.
passages.sermon:
A mixed group of people went with the Israelites.
Many animals went with them.
They took large flocks of sheep.
They took many herds of cattle.
They had a great amount of livestock.
passages.original: וְגַם־ עֵ֥רֶב רַ֖ב עָלָ֣ה אִתָּ֑ם וְצֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר מִקְנֶ֖ה כָּבֵ֥ד מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Since their dough had no leaven, the people baked what they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened loaves. For when they had been driven out of Egypt, they could not delay and had not prepared any provisions for themselves.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites left Egypt in a hurry.
They took dough with them from Egypt.
The dough had no leaven in it.
They baked the dough into flat, unleavened loaves.
They had been forced to leave Egypt quickly.
They could not wait.
They did not have time to prepare food for themselves.
passages.original: וַיֹּאפ֨וּ אֶת־ הַבָּצֵ֜ק אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצִ֧יאוּ מִמִּצְרַ֛יִם עֻגֹ֥ת מַצּ֖וֹת כִּ֣י לֹ֣א חָמֵ֑ץ כִּֽי־ גֹרְשׁ֣וּ מִמִּצְרַ֗יִם וְלֹ֤א יָֽכְלוּ֙ לְהִתְמַהְמֵ֔הַּ וְגַם־ צֵדָ֖ה לֹא־ עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Now the duration of the Israelites’ stay in Egypt was 430 years.
passages.sermon: The Israelites lived in Egypt.\r\nThey stayed there for 430 years.
passages.original: וּמוֹשַׁב֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשְׁב֖וּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: At the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the LORD’s divisions went out of the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites lived in Egypt for 430 years.
God is the LORD.
God had many people in Egypt.
God called these people His divisions.
After 430 years ended, God acted.
On that exact day, all the LORD’s divisions left Egypt.
God brought His people out of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י מִקֵּץ֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֶ֙צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה יָֽצְא֛וּ כָּל־ צִבְא֥וֹת יְהוָ֖ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Because the LORD kept a vigil that night to bring them out of the land of Egypt, this same night is to be a vigil to the LORD, to be observed by all the Israelites for the generations to come.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD watched over the Israelites that night.
The LORD brought the Israelites out of Egypt that night.
That night belongs to the LORD.
The Israelites must keep watch on that night.
All generations of Israelites must observe this night for the LORD.
passages.original: לֵ֣יל שִׁמֻּרִ֥ים הוּא֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לְהוֹצִיאָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הֽוּא־ הַלַּ֤יְלָה הַזֶּה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה שִׁמֻּרִ֛ים לְכָל־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃פ

passages.text: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the statute of the Passover: No foreigner is to eat of it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
The LORD gave them a command about the Passover.
This is the rule for the Passover.
No foreigner may eat the Passover meal.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן זֹ֖את חֻקַּ֣ת הַפָּ֑סַח כָּל־ בֶּן־ נֵכָ֖ר לֹא־ יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But any slave who has been purchased may eat of it, after you have circumcised him.
passages.sermon: A man may purchase a slave with money.\r\nYou must circumcise the purchased slave.\r\nAfter you circumcise him, the slave may eat the Passover.
passages.original: וְכָל־ עֶ֥בֶד אִ֖ישׁ מִקְנַת־ כָּ֑סֶף וּמַלְתָּ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ אָ֖ז יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: A temporary resident or hired hand shall not eat the Passover.
passages.sermon: A temporary resident must not eat the Passover.\r\nA hired worker must not eat the Passover.
passages.original: תּוֹשָׁ֥ב וְשָׂכִ֖יר לֹא־ יֹ֥אכַל־ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: It must be eaten inside one house. You are not to take any of the meat outside the house, and you may not break any of the bones.
passages.sermon: The Passover meal must be eaten inside one house.\r\nDo not take any of the meat outside the house.\r\nDo not break any of the bones.
passages.original: בְּבַ֤יִת אֶחָד֙ יֵאָכֵ֔ל לֹא־ תוֹצִ֧יא מִן־ הַבַּ֛יִת מִן־ הַבָּשָׂ֖ר ח֑וּצָה וְעֶ֖צֶם לֹ֥א תִשְׁבְּרוּ־ בֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The whole congregation of Israel must celebrate it.
passages.sermon: The people of Israel are a congregation.\r\nGod commands the whole congregation of Israel.\r\nEvery person in the congregation must celebrate the Passover.
passages.original: כָּל־ עֲדַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יַעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If a foreigner resides with you and wants to celebrate the LORD’s Passover, all the males in the household must be circumcised; then he may come near to celebrate it, and he shall be like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised man may eat of it.
passages.sermon:
A foreigner may live among you.
This foreigner may want to celebrate the LORD’s Passover.
All the males in his household must be circumcised first.
After this, the foreigner may come near to celebrate the Passover.
He will be like a native of the land.
No uncircumcised man may eat the Passover.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יָג֨וּר אִתְּךָ֜ גֵּ֗ר וְעָ֣שָׂה פֶסַח֮ לַיהוָה֒ הִמּ֧וֹל ל֣וֹ כָל־ זָכָ֗ר וְאָז֙ יִקְרַ֣ב לַעֲשֹׂת֔וֹ וְהָיָ֖ה כְּאֶזְרַ֣ח הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכָל־ עָרֵ֖ל לֹֽא־ יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The same law shall apply to both the native and the foreigner who resides among you.”
passages.sermon:
God gave a law to Israel.
This law applies to every native Israelite.
This law also applies to every foreigner who lives among the Israelites.
God makes one law for both the native and the foreigner.
passages.original: תּוֹרָ֣ה אַחַ֔ת יִהְיֶ֖ה לָֽאֶזְרָ֑ח וְלַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֥ר בְּתוֹכְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then all the Israelites did this—they did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
passages.sermon:
All the Israelites acted.
The Israelites followed the LORD’s command.
The LORD gave commands to Moses and Aaron.
The Israelites did exactly what the LORD told Moses and Aaron.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֖וּ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽת־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃ס

passages.text: And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has great power.
The Israelites are God’s chosen people.
Egypt is a foreign land where the Israelites lived as slaves.
On that very day, the LORD acted.
The LORD brought the Israelites out of Egypt.
The Israelites left Egypt in their groups.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י בְּעֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה הוֹצִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל־ צִבְאֹתָֽם׃פ
